page.title: Cresta Sassal Mason (2847 m) — Hike Plan

hero.subtitle_html: Photo © Walter Micheletti (CC BY 3.0) — Piz Palü glacier and Bernina Railway

intro_html: Dramatic glacier and peak views of Piz Palü along a spectacular alpine balcony. Walk alongside the UNESCO-listed Bernina Railway, one of Switzerland's most scenic train routes.

routes.title_html: Cresta Sassal Mason via Alpine Balcony — Start at Ospizio San Gottardo (2064 m) on the Bernina Pass. Follow the trail along the eastern slopes of Piz Palü, staying high on the alpine balcony. Ascend gradually via glacier-exposed terrain to the Cresta Sassal Mason ridge. Summit climb with exposure; snow/ice likely until late summer.

getting_there.by_pt_html: Bernina Railway (UNESCO heritage line): Take the RhB Bernina Express or regional train from Chur → Tirano, then return to Switzerland. Alight at Ospizio San Gottardo station on the Bernina line. Journey time ~2–2.5 hours from Chur.
getting_there.by_car_html: From Chur head south via A13 towards Tirano (Italy). Follow signs to Poschiavo. Park at Ospizio San Gottardo (2064 m) on the Bernina Pass. (Note: Pass is typically open June–October; check road conditions in winter.)

day_plans.title: Day 1
rows: Depart Ospizio San Gottardo (2064m); early start for optimal lighting on glacier
Reach Alp Grum area (~2100m); begin Bernina terrain ascent
Arrive Piz Palü glacial base (~2400m); glacier views & railway context
Enter Cresta ridge approach (2600m+); exposure increases
Alpine scramble toward Sassal Mason; final 250m vertical
Summit Cresta Sassal Mason (2847m); total ~4 hours up
Return to Ospizio San Gottardo; ~7 hours total

weather.season_html: July–September is best; June often has residual snow/ice on ridges. Avoid after fresh snow—avalanche risk and whiteout conditions.

takeaways_html: Glacier terrain & crevasse hazards: Route crosses or approaches Piz Palü glacial zone; late spring/early summer requires rope team & crampons. Summer conditions more stable but require route-finding skill.
Bernina Railway UNESCO heritage context: Red-line train passes continuously through the valley; iconic photogenic vantage point. Trail timing can sync with train departures for photography.

Weather & rockfall exposure: High altitude (2847m) + exposed ridge + glacial hangings make this a serious alpine route. Afternoon thunderstorms can develop rapidly. Rockfall risk from warming glacial slopes in mid-summer.

gear.title: Essential
items_html:
• Hiking poles
  • Sun protection (cream + glasses + hat)
  • 2 L water
  • Emergency snacks

safety_html: Glacier exposure & crevasses: Route crosses active glacial terrain; crevasse fall risk requires rope team & technical rescue capability. Late spring/early summer particularly hazardous.
Exposure & scrambling (T3+): Ridge sections involve hand-holds & exposed terrain; unroped scrambling with 300m+ cliff drops. Sure-footedness mandatory.
Weather deterioration: Rapid visibility loss; afternoon thunderstorm risk extreme at 2847m. Exposed ridge offers zero shelter.
Rockfall: Warming glacial slopes (mid-July–August) increase rockfall from above; loose rock on descent.
Route-finding: Cairns sparse; GPS/map essential in poor visibility. Glacier navigation complex without mountaineering experience.
Turn back if thunderstorms develop — lightning risk above treeline is extreme.
